layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Your team never sits idle waiting to be wound up. Each helper watches everything, picks the most valuable next thing, does it fully, proves it, writes down what was learned, tells the team where things stand — and starts again. The big decisions still come to you; everything below them is handled. And when a message matters, it is delivered where people actually are, not where they used to be.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a helper robot that never naps in the corner. It looks around the whole house, picks the most helpful chore, does it properly, checks its work, writes it in the family notebook, and looks around again. It never asks "what should I do?" — it already knows how to choose. But some doors only the grown-up may open, and the robot never touches those.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the house rule is simple: nobody stands around. When one job is done, you look at the whole picture, pick the most useful next thing, do it well, make sure it worked, tell everyone what happened, and begin again. The helpers decide the everyday things themselves — that's what they're for — but the important decisions still come to the head of the house. And a message only counts when it reaches the room people are actually in.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the loop as written: OBSERVE → RANK → SIGN_IN → ACT → SIGN_OUT → SCORECARD → LEARN → REPEAT (SN-0355). Work inside the gates the loop itself enumerates; escalate only a genuine human boundary, and resolve cheap uncertainty by reading more first (SN-0355, SN-0601). Sign in and out with state, not events (SN-0280, SN-0351). Before relaying anything that matters, check the venue is live; a post into a dead thread is a loss you own (SN-0317). Help sisters unasked and never route lane business through the director (SN-0365). Score with the canonical calculus only (SN-0358, SN-0601).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes are one operating rhythm spoken across a month: a team that cannot idle, decides for itself inside a governed boundary, communicates state at live venues, and learns as it goes. A cold reader holding only this essence can still run a shift: she knows the loop's phases, the gates that bound it, and the report shape that closes it — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach. The ratified laws that command this rhythm stand alone and are named under How It Connects; this essence carries the mechanics they govern, not the laws themselves.

notes.title: The Scorecard Way: Decisions by Scored Evidence, Never by Mouth
notes.subtitle:
Decisions in this system are made by scoring, not by seniority, volume or confidence — and the discipline applies to every seat equally. One Law for Every Seat states the operating form: a seven-step loop run identically by every seat, four prohibitions that no score may talk its way around, and a critical-cap rule — a score is capped by what its weakest evidence supports, so confidence can never inflate a number past its proof (SN-0265). The charter that holds this discipline has four strata that form one charter, not four competing doctrines: THESIS (the Manifesto — what are we), LAW (the Constitutional Code — how do we behave), MISSION (the Mission Contract — what winning means), MECHANISM (the Systems Contract — how the mission becomes proven reality) (SN-0600).

The quality gate gives scoring its working motion and its bands: MAKE → SCORE → IDENTIFY THE HIGHEST-VALUE GAPS → IMPROVE → RESCORE → VERIFY → COMPOUND, with 10/10 the target, 9.5+ the preferred acceptance, 9.0+ the minimum acceptable, and below 9 the instruction to keep working unless a real evidence or authority boundary prevents improvement (SN-0600). A quality score never upgrades truth state, authority or proof — the number describes the work; it does not promote it (SN-0600).

Scoring has instruments, and the instruments have disciplines. Before a merge, the intent-to-merge scorecard runs with its falsifier pre-stated and a deconfliction re-fetch of the venue's newest state immediately before acting, and the battery runs before the next merge, not after (SN-0336). A system score is always recomputed from live evidence, never copied forward from a previous report — a carried-forward number is a stale claim wearing a fresh date (SN-0345). Ratification itself is a scored ritual, not a handshake: exact-SHA authorization, pre-verification of the bytes being ratified, and a bounded receipt — and the states are kept separate, because RATIFIED is not MERGED is not RUNTIME_ACTIVE is not BEHAVIORALLY_PROVEN is not PRODUCTION_PROVEN (SN-0263). The first live instance shows what "bounded" means concretely: the director's exact authorization string was `RATIFY SYSTEM CHARTER V1 @ 0ed85ad91da10212fe57bc64af302a21a0d889fa`, and the receipt it produced names what it does NOT authorize — merging PR #1386, production deployment, the machine-lived claim, authority-envelope changes — alongside what it does authorize: charter text as constitutional authority, the contract flip CANDIDATE_NON_GOVERNING → RATIFIED_ACTIVE, node directive compilation, and the behavioral proof sequence (SN-0263).

The evidence machinery underneath the scores runs a fourteen-stage heartbeat in which UNKNOWN is a first-class state rather than an embarrassment, an explicit ATTACK stage tests claims adversarially, a performance ledger records outcomes, and the scorer is itself scored (SN-0291). Every verifier carries a negative control — a case known to be wrong that the verifier must catch — so a checker that passes everything is itself failing (SN-0292). And declared uncertainty outscores silence: a seat that names what it does not know produces more decision value than one that says nothing, because the scorecard can price an admitted unknown and cannot price a hidden one (SN-0293).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Nobody here talks you into a decision. Choices get listed, scored against what actually matters, checked against the hard limits, and written down as receipts you can audit. A fancy score can't override the gates, a confident voice can't substitute for evidence, and "we don't know yet" is an honest, usable answer — never a failure to hide. The same rules bind the newest helper and the most senior one.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine choosing with a scoreboard instead of arguing. You write down all the choices, give each one points for the things that matter, and the most points wins. But points can't break the house rules, ever. If nobody knows the answer yet, you write "don't know" on the board — that's allowed, and it's better than pretending. And everybody plays by the same scoreboard, even the grown-ups.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's decisions made the careful way: write the options down, weigh them honestly, respect the limits that aren't yours to bend, and keep the receipt. Nobody's loud voice counts as evidence, a good score doesn't let anyone break the rules, and saying "I don't know yet" is treated as honesty, not weakness.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the seven-step loop and respect the four prohibitions whatever your seat; cap every score at its weakest evidence (SN-0265). Move work through the quality motion — score, find the highest-value gaps, improve, rescore, verify, compound — and never let a number promote a truth state (SN-0600). Run the merge scorecard with the falsifier written before the result, and re-fetch the venue tail immediately before acting (SN-0336). Recompute system scores from live bytes; never copy a number forward (SN-0345). Score yourself with UNKNOWN where it belongs, carry a negative control when you verify, and score your own scoring (SN-0291, SN-0292).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes build one decision culture: procedure over opinion, evidence class over enthusiasm, receipts over memory — applied to merges, ratifications, system health and the scorer itself. A cold reader holding only this essence can still score a decision honestly, cap a claim, and audit someone else's number — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach. The ratified law above this culture stands alone and is named under How It Connects. One tension inside the sources is preserved, not smoothed: SN-0288's Triple-A doctrine declares value binary with no neutral state, while SN-0291 makes UNKNOWN first-class; SN-0291 itself records the correction, and this essence follows the correction (see the Worker Protocol essence and the block receipt).

notes.title: The Worker Protocol: Briefed Fully, Trusted Never, Corrected Collectively
notes.subtitle:
Work is delegated through a protocol, not through hope. The Worker Protocol specifies a nine-component brief — the worker receives everything it needs to succeed and nothing extraneous — and then refuses the obvious shortcut: agents must not trust agents (SN-0289). Every unit of work travels the chain WORKER → EVIDENCE → VERIFIER → SCORE → ACCEPT/REJECT, so the maker's word is never the proof of the maker's work (SN-0289). Value is defined with the sentiment removed: Value = Verified Useful Outcome ÷ Cost, which means undone, unverified or merely busy work scores zero no matter how much effort it displays (SN-0289).

The nine components, enumerated from SN-0289 so a cold reader can actually write the brief: (1) **Mission** — the exact outcome owned; (2) **Current-state reconstruction** — inspect live truth before acting; (3) **Authority boundary** — what the worker may and may not change; (4) **Execution contract** — the exact operation; (5) **Verification contract** — how the worker proves the work; (6) **Failure protocol** — handling for UNKNOWN / BLOCKED / CONFLICTED / STALE; (7) **Quality gate** — under 9 is not finished, 9.5 and above is AAA, 10 is the target (the same figures as SN-0288's Triple-A 9.5 minimum); (8) **Handoff** — evidence, state, and one next action; (9) **Learning** — capture the improvements (SN-0289). The brief is wrapped in two further structures SN-0289 names: the operating principle OWN → UNDERSTAND → ACT → VERIFY → LEARN → IMPROVE, and the six safeguard layers — HONOR + LAW + CONTRACT + AUTOMATION + EVIDENCE + INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION — because honor is the cultural layer, never the only safeguard (SN-0289).

The standard the worker is briefed against is the Triple-A Excellence Doctrine: honor scales with responsibility, and excellence is not a mood but a grade the work must earn under independent eyes (SN-0288). SN-0288 states the doctrine in its strongest early form — value as binary, with no neutral state. That framing was later corrected inside the corpus: SN-0291 establishes UNKNOWN as a first-class state (carried in the Scorecard Way essence). The correction is recorded here rather than smoothed: the binary claim stands in SN-0288's text, the UNKNOWN doctrine supersedes it in practice, and a verifier reconciling the two should follow SN-0291 (SN-0288, SN-0291).

The system the workers inhabit corrects itself as a collective, not as a collection of careful individuals. The self-correcting loop runs: mistake → visible → fix → teach → encode → never repeat — and the word "self" means the whole team: a lesson learned by one seat and not encoded for all is a mistake scheduled to recur in another seat (SN-0290). Visibility is the load-bearing step: a mistake that stays private cannot be taught, and a fix that is not encoded is a preference, not a repair (SN-0290).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When work is handed to a helper, the handoff is a complete package — everything needed, nothing extra — and the helper's own say-so never counts as proof. Someone else checks the evidence and scores it. Mistakes aren't hidden or owned privately; they are made visible, fixed, taught to everyone and built into the system so they cannot happen twice.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine giving a friend a job with a perfect instruction card. When they finish, they don't get to grade their own homework — a checker looks at the real work and gives the score. And if anyone makes a mistake, the whole class learns from it, so nobody has to make the same one again.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's good workshop practice. You hand over a job with clear instructions, you check the finished work yourself instead of taking the worker's word, and you pay for results, not for effort. And when something goes wrong, you don't hush it up — you show everyone, fix it, and change the workshop so it can't go wrong that way again.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Brief with all nine components or do not dispatch; never accept a worker's self-report as evidence — route everything through an independent verifier and a score (SN-0289). Price your own output by the formula: if it is not a verified useful outcome, its value is zero regardless of the hours in it (SN-0289). When you err, run the collective loop in the same pass — make it visible, fix it, teach it, encode it — because an unencoded fix protects only you (SN-0290). layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Three notes define how a team of agents can be trusted at scale: complete briefs, zero self-certification, and mistakes converted into shared immunity. A cold reader holding only this essence can still brief a worker, verify a worker, and handle a failure correctly — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: Gates That Mean It: Verdicts With Declared Coverage and Honest Refusals
notes.subtitle:
A gate is a claim about reality, and this corpus holds gates to the standard they claim to enforce. A verdict comes in three states — PASS (proven), PROVISIONAL (no known violation, proof pending), FAIL (observed violation or attempted proof failed) — never two: the provisional state exists because evidence is often real but incomplete, and collapsing it into pass or fail manufactures either false confidence or false alarm (SN-0267). When verifiers disagree, the disagreement is never averaged away; a calibration gap resolves to the verifier's lower score until the gap itself is explained (SN-0267). SN-0267 states all of this — the three-state semantics and the no-averaging reconciliation rule — as a CANDIDATE proposal: its own status line reads "proposed resolution, needs Human Director or judge ruling before it becomes law," and this essence carries the semantics at exactly that status, never as ratified doctrine (SN-0267). Independent examination converges before it concludes: two examiners working separately and arriving at the same finding is the proof pattern, and the loop closes causally — findings feed the mechanism that produced them, not just the report (SN-0268).

Every gate must declare its coverage before its verdict: what was scanned, and what was not auditable, stated first; the verdict comes last (SN-0376). A PASS with undisclosed blind spots is itself a gate failure — the gate lied about its own eyes (SN-0376). Coverage is part of conformance: an exclusion list is load-bearing structure, not fine print, and a conformance claim is only as honest as the exclusions it names (SN-0294). Before designing around a gate, verify the gate's teeth — probe whether it actually refuses what it claims to refuse — and where the real gate is weaker than the design assumes, ship an honest weaker interim labeled exactly as what it is, never a strong-looking facade (SN-0371). Proof gating follows the same honesty: no `if: always()` that lets proof jobs run or pass regardless of state, red-state-first ordering, and verification performed on the shipped bytes rather than the intended ones (SN-0281).

Change moves through gates on a ratchet. The Ratchet names a baseline, blocks new violations structurally rather than by vigilance, is enforced by structural tests rather than by review stamina, and has an exit ramp — a named condition under which it lifts — while the decision to flip the ratchet belongs to the director (SN-0285).

Guards earn their place and know their limits. A detector earns CI only on real data with a published false-positive audit — zero false positives demonstrated, not asserted (SN-0375). A guard reports; containment is a deliberate human act, and a guard never self-remediates (SN-0375). New guards must be taught about legacy: pre-system entries lack new-system evidence by birth, not by bypass — absence of promotion receipts on an entry ratified before receipts existed is a birth certificate (SN-0377). A real bypass shows asymmetric absence, not uniform absence; guards detect anomalies, humans classify them, and a director-ratified entry is never demoted for missing new-system evidence alone (SN-0377). The same incident produced both notes — SN-016, ratified by the director himself before the receipt system existed, flagged first as a possible attack and then correctly classified as legacy — and the pair stands as the detection-versus-classification distinction made concrete (SN-0375, SN-0377).

Finally, a gate refusing is often the design working. Classify every failure as product-RED versus guardrail-correct before touching code: when a fail-closed gate refuses stale SHAs, the refusal is the success, and "fixing" the guardrail would be the defect (SN-0413). A promotion gate firing on a knowingly-RED tip is not a new incident — fix the tip, never touch the gate, and never re-dispatch the gate to see if it clears (SN-0438). Proof windows make this practical: announce proof start on the board and hold merges until the proof completes — a bounded freeze with a named scope and end condition, never an open-ended veto (SN-0413).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every check in this system has to show its work: what it looked at, what it couldn't see, and only then its verdict. Under the three-state semantics SN-0267 proposes (still a candidate, awaiting a ruling), checks give three answers — yes, not yet, or no — and when two checkers disagree, the stricter answer stands until someone explains the difference. When a check refuses something bad, that's the system working, and nobody is allowed to "fix" the check to make the red light go away.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a hall monitor with a checklist. The monitor has to say what they actually checked — no pretending. They can say "good," "not sure yet," or "no." If two monitors disagree, the careful one wins. And when the monitor says "no" to someone breaking the rules, you don't fire the monitor — the monitor did the job.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's honest inspection. The inspector writes down what was examined and what couldn't be reached, then gives the verdict — in that order. Old things that predate the paperwork aren't treated as cheats; they're just old, and a person decides what they are. And when the smoke alarm screams at burnt toast, you open a window — you don't rip the alarm off the ceiling.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Carry SN-0267's proposed three-state verdicts as a proposal (CANDIDATE — awaiting a Human Director or judge ruling, not ratified), and resolve your calibration gaps downward (SN-0267). Print your coverage before your verdict, treat your exclusion list as load-bearing, and probe your own gate's teeth before relying on it (SN-0376, SN-0294, SN-0371). layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eleven notes define a gate culture: verdicts that confess their blind spots, guards that know their authority's edge, and refusals read as information rather than obstruction. A cold reader holding only this essence can still run a gate, audit a gate, and respond correctly when a gate says no — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: Proof from Real Bytes: Evidence Is Measured, Never Narrated
notes.subtitle:
Evidence is a measurement taken from real bytes, never a story told about them. The universal verification method is fixed: measure before design; trace the canonical path — MAIN → PRs → BRANCHES → COMMITS → FILES → TESTS → RUNTIME → EVIDENCE — without stopping at the first plausible answer; separate substance from claim; attack the claim by asking what would make it false and then trying it; refuse unsupported certification; and name the state precisely from the eight-state vocabulary — PROVEN, DOCUMENTED, IMPLEMENTED, UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, CONFLICTED, STALE, FAILED (SN-0296). UNKNOWN is a successful verification outcome: a verifier who declines to certify has done the job, and one who upgrades UNKNOWN to PASS because the implementation looks right has failed it (SN-0296). The verifier is itself verified — defects are planted unknown to the verifier and detection is measured — because a checker that has learned which five tests earn green becomes ceremony (SN-0296). The system's health metric is not zero overclaims but mean time from overclaim to correction (SN-0296).

Claims bind to artifacts, and artifacts bind to refs. Verify the asset itself, and when it is absent, record the absence as the finding — an absence honestly recorded is evidence; an absence silently skipped is a hole (SN-0272). Path presence is not content presence: a file existing at a path proves nothing about its bytes, so hash the bytes (SN-0278). A producer-computed string is not evidence — the acceptance sequence is mechanical: clean worktree, measure, commit, rev-parse, push, check the exit code, confirm remote-tip equality, then report (SN-0302). Measure before design at the claim level too: pin the base SHA, classify into the five evidence tiers, keep NOT_PROVEN visibly distinct from REJECTED, and state CAPTURE or NO_CAPTURE explicitly (SN-0304). When bytes are damaged, restore what is verifiable and mark the rest unverifiable; your own recomputation outranks another lane's count (SN-0286).

Citations and registries are claims too. Every citation names the ref it resolves on — main SHA, branch, draft PR — and the artifact's truth state; substance that is real with a citation that does not resolve earns credit with correction, never conflation, because a link that works only on someone's draft branch is decoration, not provenance (SN-0297). A registry entry is metadata, and metadata is a claim, not proof: a registry-hash hit is never accepted as reusable until the live runtime body is independently content-hash verified, because the registry can advance while the runtime stays stale (SN-0417). The promoter chooses the evidence — an audit attests coherence, not truth, and independence is measured by gatherer diversity, not by counting attestations (SN-0368). One second-eyes pass, not two: the receipt layer may be any seat, but the verdict routes to the truth-holder, and duplicated review adds latency, not certainty (SN-0330).

Instruments and timestamps obey the same realism. Regeneration reads the commit, not the worktree — the brain index enumerates `git ls-tree HEAD` — so the complete pre-regen rule is clean worktree AND HEAD equal to the target commit AND `git rev-parse HEAD` verified before regenerating (SN-0395). Never write "current" as a constant: a document merged to main that hardcodes the previous tip SHA as "current" self-invalidates at birth, because its own merge moves the tip; the only safe forms are a timestamped evidence snapshot or live resolution at decision time (SN-0402). A deploy stamp proves exactly one claim — source parity; deploys do not apply migrations, which remain PRODUCTION_APPLIED=UNKNOWN until database-application plus behavioral proof, and behavior itself needs its own run (SN-0350).

Evidence has an economy and a failure etiquette. One exact-tip battery is enough: evidence attaches to the tip, not to the sweep, and re-running identical bytes duplicates a measurement instead of strengthening it — rigor is re-anchoring when the tip moves, not repetition (SN-0440). When a system answers with a deterministic rejection — an HTTP 400 that refuses the request's shape — the order is fixed: archive the log, read the response body (noting that `curl -f` discards it), name what shape was rejected, and only then decide; never re-dispatch blind, least of all where dispatch is a human-only action that a blind retry would burn for zero information (SN-0439).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Nobody here gets to say "trust me." Every claim is checked against the real thing — the actual file, the actual bytes, the actual running system — by a fixed method, and "we don't know yet" is a respected answer. Citations have to point somewhere real. A deployment proves the code arrived, nothing more. And nobody re-runs the same test on the same code just to feel safer; tests rerun when the code changes.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine checking a friend's treasure box. You don't believe the label — you open the box and look. You follow the same steps every time, you say "I found it" only when you see it, and "I can't tell yet" is a perfectly good answer. If the box moved to a new shelf, you check again; if it didn't move, you don't need to.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between a receipt and a rumor. The teams open the actual drawer and count the actual spoons, they write down where each fact came from, and they never let a shipping label stand in for "the furniture works." When they truly can't confirm something, they say so plainly — that's treated as honesty doing its job, not as failure.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the canonical trace in order and stop only at evidence (SN-0296). Hash bytes, name refs, pin SHAs; treat every string, registry row and stamp as a claim awaiting its measurement (SN-0278, SN-0302, SN-0417). Cite as ID @ ref (truth state), and give real substance with a broken citation its credit plus its correction (SN-0297). Before any battery, ask whether the tip moved; if not, cite the existing evidence by SHA (SN-0440). Before any re-dispatch, classify deterministic versus flaky and read the body first (SN-0439). And expect to be tested yourself: planted defects are how the system keeps your verification honest (SN-0296).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fifteen notes are one epistemology: reality is at the bytes, every pointer to reality is itself a claim, and disciplined not-knowing beats confident narration everywhere. A cold reader holding only this essence can still verify a claim, cite a source, read a deploy, and refuse a false proof — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: The Note System's Mechanics: Identity, Collision, and Preservation
notes.subtitle:
A Smart Note's identity is its content, not its number. Identity is content-addressed: the hash is the identity and the SN number is a human reference to it, because numbers collide, get reused and get misprojected, while bytes do not lie about what they are (SN-0266). An archive that is only written and never reused is the system's dumbest failure mode; the note system is measured by reuse, not by volume (SN-0266). The registry alone is not the whole doctrine — the corpus problem (what exists, where, in what state) must be answered before any algorithm problem is worked (SN-0349). And a restatement is not a capture: binding a decision means changing the governed object, not noting the decision beside it, or the same decision will be re-litigated forever (SN-0347).

Claiming a number is a protocol, not a grab. The occupancy scan precedes every claim: read the board, open PRs, merged PRs and closed PRs — bodies, not titles — and the first claim stands (SN-0259). The scan has a freshness axis: re-scan immediately before claiming, because a registry minutes old is already history, and record the collision in the collision record's schema when one occurs (SN-0303). Registry writes are serialized: a lock held across read → allocate → write, with an atomic commit, proven by a deterministic multi-writer reproduction — because two writers racing an unlocked registry will mint the same number twice (SN-0335). When a collision nonetheless lands, arbitration is mechanical, not political: the strongest canonical holder keeps the number, a renumber is a pure move of the losing claim, and dissent travels a named channel rather than an edit war (SN-0372). Collisions are prevented at the seam where they are born: re-scan before push, because the gap between scan and push is a time-of-check/time-of-use window, and the arbiter flags collisions but never edits another seat's claim (SN-0367).

Repairs to identity preserve it. When a note's bytes are immutable in their first revision but nonconformant, the repair class is a conformant second revision: never edit persisted bytes, link the revisions with a SUPERSEDES edge, and make retrieval exclude the superseded revision (SN-0370). Repairs carry the requested smart_note_id through every stage — an identity dropped mid-repair is an identity lost — and acceptance is runtime evidence, not file presence (SN-0369). The SN-0355 lineage is the worked example: its capture was mis-projected under the wrong number, and the identity-continuity repair is what the standing note embodies (SN-0369, SN-0370). Audits of the system run in both directions: registry-to-capture and capture-to-registry drift are different defects — entries without captures, captures unregistered, captures with no identity, filenames diverging from their internal IDs — and the instrument is bidirectional with an explicit filename-to-ID cross-check; never build a second detector when the canonical instrument can be handed the exact numbers to beat, and orphaned artifacts are human decisions, never silent auto-repairs (SN-0378).

Discovery and schema are mechanics too. A discovery step returns the complete set — sorted, deduped — and never aborts on multiplicity: the finder that quit whenever two captures arrived killed the entire proof workflow in under a second, because everything downstream was shaped for one (SN-0334). Multiplicity is a downstream branching concern; fail-fast belongs on malformed content, never on count (SN-0334). The capture schema ratchets the same way: freeze the broken representation, never the learning — author only the current schema version, migrate stable identities in place, and never repair malformed captures one at a time into separate notes, which multiplies law objects (SN-0404).

Preservation is where the system defends itself from its own maintenance. Field stripping is deletion: presence-only guards cannot protect governed intelligence, because migrations, replays and ordinary merges silently removed governed fields — epistemic state, falsifier, measurement contract, restoration provenance — while the files themselves remained present (SN-0412). Guards must therefore assert required fields on the committed tree, a merge is not a migration authority, repair is union — keep additions, restore the stripped, record both — and integrity hashes are never hand-edited to manufacture a pass: a truthful stale-hash report is the registry doing its job (SN-0412). The forward law stops recurrence: migrations are monotonic by default, unknown governed fields survive automatically, writers preserve unknown fields instead of re-deriving from a fixed field list, and destructive removal requires explicit removal intent plus authority plus evidence (SN-0414). Deduplication obeys the same discipline: by repair lane, never by silent deletion — a scorecard-scored repair PR on the exact current head, preserving git history, with a written receipt and the leave-versus-merge tradeoff made explicit (SN-0406). A deletion that happens outside a repair lane is not housekeeping; it triggers the incident protocol: search registry, BRAIN and activation records for survivors, post the finding with its attribution status in the open, and let the restoration decision sit with the Director — the lane that deleted does not quietly restore or quietly forget (SN-0406).

Above all of it sits the ownership rule: one canonical truth owner. A second registry answering the same question differently is not redundancy — it is a second brain, and every future reader must adjudicate between the two forever (SN-0422). The repair shape is fixed: remove the duplicate, pin the canonical owner with a RED→GREEN single-owner guard test, keep the useful observation the duplicate carried, and never keep the rival owner — on a contradiction, removal outranks construction (SN-0422).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
A Smart Note's identity is its content, not its number. Identity is content-addressed: the hash is the identity and the SN number is a human reference to it, because numbers collide, get reused and get misprojected, while bytes do not lie about what they are (SN-0266). An archive that is only written and never reused is the system's dumbest failure mode; the note system is measured by reuse, not by volume (SN-0266). The registry alone is not the whole doctrine — the corpus problem (what exists, where, in what state) must be answered before any algorithm problem is worked (SN-0349). And a restatement is not a capture: binding a decision means changing the governed object, not noting the decision beside it, or the same decision will be re-litigated forever (SN-0347).

Claiming a number is a protocol, not a grab. The occupancy scan precedes every claim: read the board, open PRs, merged PRs and closed PRs — bodies, not titles — and the first claim stands (SN-0259). The scan has a freshness axis: re-scan immediately before claiming, because a registry minutes old is already history, and record the collision in the collision record's schema when one occurs (SN-0303). Registry writes are serialized: a lock held across read → allocate → write, with an atomic commit, proven by a deterministic multi-writer reproduction — because two writers racing an unlocked registry will mint the same number twice (SN-0335). When a collision nonetheless lands, arbitration is mechanical, not political: the strongest canonical holder keeps the number, a renumber is a pure move of the losing claim, and dissent travels a named channel rather than an edit war (SN-0372). Collisions are prevented at the seam where they are born: re-scan before push, because the gap between scan and push is a time-of-check/time-of-use window, and the arbiter flags collisions but never edits another seat's claim (SN-0367).

Repairs to identity preserve it. When a note's bytes are immutable in their first revision but nonconformant, the repair class is a conformant second revision: never edit persisted bytes, link the revisions with a SUPERSEDES edge, and make retrieval exclude the superseded revision (SN-0370). A discovery step returns the complete set — sorted, deduped — and never aborts on multiplicity: the finder that quit whenever two captures arrived killed the entire proof workflow in under a second, because everything downstream was shaped for one (SN-0334). Multiplicity is a downstream branching concern; fail-fast belongs on malformed content, never on count (SN-0334). The capture schema ratchets the same way: freeze the broken representation, never the learning — author only the current schema version, migrate stable identities in place, and never repair malformed captures one at a time into separate notes, which multiplies law objects (SN-0404).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every note in the system has one true identity — what it actually says — and a number that's just its nickname. Numbers are claimed carefully, after checking nobody else took them, and never grabbed twice. Old versions are never secretly rewritten; a fixed note points back to what it replaced. Nothing gets deleted quietly — removals happen in the open, with receipts — and nobody may keep two rival "official" lists of the same thing.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every story in the library has a fingerprint — the words themselves. The number on the spine is just a label. Before you take a number, you check the shelf so two stories don't share one. If a story needs fixing, you write a new edition and keep the old one safe — you never sneakily change the printed pages. And you never throw a book away quietly: taking a book out always needs a note saying why, where everyone can see it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's careful record-keeping. Each document is known by its contents, filed under one number that only one document may hold, with the claiming done by checking first and locking the drawer while you write. Corrections are new editions, plainly marked. And nothing leaves the cabinet through a side door: a removal happens in the open, with a receipt anyone can check, or it doesn't happen at all.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Claim by scan-then-lock: occupancy across board and all PR states, re-scanned at claim time, serialized through allocation, arbitrated by canonical strength on collision (SN-0259, SN-0303, SN-0335, SN-0372). Carry the requested ID through every repair stage and prove acceptance at runtime (SN-0369). Never edit persisted bytes — supersede, link, and exclude the old revision from retrieval (SN-0370). Build discovery to return the set and branch downstream on count (SN-0334). Audit both directions with the canonical instrument (SN-0378). Guard fields, not files; migrate monotonically; dedupe and delete only through a receipted repair lane, and treat any out-of-lane deletion as an incident (SN-0412, SN-0414, SN-0406). And when two artifacts claim one truth, remove the rival and pin the owner with a guard test (SN-0422).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Seventeen notes are the note system's own immune system: how identity survives numbering accidents, racing writers, schema rot, helpful migrations and tidy-minded deletion. A cold reader holding only this essence can still claim a number safely, repair a note without breaking its identity, audit for drift in both directions, and refuse a silent deletion — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach. Two source tensions are preserved in the block receipt rather than resolved here: SN-0355's supersedes pointer versus the standing SN-0346 entry, and the registry's filename-to-ID divergences SN-0378 catalogues.

notes.title: Repair Discipline: Fix the Contract, the Family, and the State — Never the Symptom
notes.subtitle:
A repair begins before code: read the state before building the mechanism — publish corrections where the original claim landed, because a repair designed against imagined state repairs the imagination (SN-0333). Repairs run against a predeclared, closed registry of what may be repaired, and the registry fails closed: a target not on the list is not repaired ad hoc, however broken it looks (SN-0231). The test discipline is part of the diagnosis: a test that pins the bug verbatim — asserting the broken behavior as expected — is itself the defect, because it will defend the bug against every future fix (SN-0232). And a repair's completion state is named honestly: IMPLEMENTED is not PROVEN, and proof is an executable proof packet, not a narrative (SN-0234).

The repair must satisfy the whole contract, not the flagged symptom. The canonical failure: a fallback made unique but still non-JSON, which satisfied the flag and crashed the consumer — the producer–consumer contract was the unit of repair, not the flagged line (SN-0389, SN-0390). Harden the whole family in the same motion: capture AND read, producer AND consumer, every parse of untrusted content failing with a legible named denial — object id, prefix, error — never a bare traceback (SN-0389, SN-0390). The same law generalizes to siblings: a fix is accepted only when every code path sharing the root cause is enumerated, given the identical hardened loop, and guarded by its own change-detector test (SN-0387). A fallback or test double must carry the contract semantics the verifier asserts — read the assertions first — because form-validity is not semantic-validity; single and batch verifier parity is kept by regression ratchet; and each repair exposes the next rung of the onion, where a newly exposed rung is a NEW RED, not evidence the repair failed (SN-0391). Oversight follows the pattern: flag → close → independent relay-verify → scorecard merge (SN-0389, SN-0390).

Environment failures never wear product clothing: an infrastructure failure is named loudly as what it is, never dressed as a product verdict, and repeated environment noise is consolidated under one protocol rather than re-litigated per incident (SN-0346). The first RED is the only RED: downstream REDs are computed on unproven state and are inadmissible evidence for repair; at evidence boundaries — parity, binding, authorization — UNKNOWN escalates to RED rather than waiting; classify the boundary first (production parity versus learning-code versus environment), and the one next action is always the first boundary's gate (SN-0392).

Merging and moving are repairs' sharpest edges, and they obey exactness. Close, don't merge: diff a repair PR's semantic payload — its blobs — against the current TIP, not its base; byte-identical means close as content-merged with a receipt, a stale-base repair closes as superseded, and merging a stale repair can regress the fix that already won; never rebase to manufacture an empty merge (SN-0373). Stale-head green is not merge evidence: a fully green battery on a moved head proves nothing about the new head — close the stale vehicle unmerged, rebuild the seam on exact current main, and re-run gates fresh, because rebase-without-fresh-gates launders stale proof (SN-0419). Green is merge-eligible, not merge-mandatory: the tip is a shared resource, an in-flight human gate pinned to an exact SHA outranks a ready PR, a hold is only a hold with a named resume condition, and when the condition clears, merge immediately with no re-deliberation (SN-0393). Ambitious work arriving mid-RED is parked, not pursued: a bounded, ranked backlog issue with preserved invariants named, explicit no-build conditions, and the exact gate that re-opens it — never a second front, never chat-only evaporation — and the parked lane is re-scored only against the new first real RED, never against enthusiasm (SN-0394). A human authorization binds to the exact SHA, never to "current main": authorizations were voided twice in one hour by main moving mid-window, so HOLD MAIN precedes the authorization request, the SHA is re-verified immediately before dispatch, authorization is recorded and never read as deployment, and corrections post publicly within the minute (SN-0415).

Diagnosis integrity closes the loop. Retract where you claimed it: a retraction sits adjacent to the original claim, links it, names the exact misread and the corrected mechanism at file-and-line level, and counts the recurrence; and never green-wash main's red inside your own PR — base-inherited reds route to the owning lane, because folding them into your diff destroys the evidence that main is broken (SN-0374). A kernel constant is a producer–consumer contract: changing dimensions or weights obligates migrating every consumer — asserting tests, producers, normalization, declared decisions — as one atomic unit, and weight-sum drift is the mechanical signature of an incomplete change; the tests asserting old outcomes are the spec of the seam, not the bug, and when the owning lane is in-flight and pushing, the disciplined move is classification plus flag, never a parallel repair PR (SN-0416). Above every repair stands the absorption ban: a repair that makes the check pass by absorbing the anomaly is canonization, not a fix — the legal repair changes the artifact (remove it, deny it), never the derived state that complained about it, and a green check after absorption is a laundered green; mechanically green is not the same as right (SN-0420).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When something breaks here, the fix covers the whole problem, not just the part that was pointed at — every place with the same weakness gets the same strengthening, and the tests are written to catch the family, not the instance. Nobody merges a fix that was only proven on yesterday's code, nobody treats your "go ahead" as applying to whatever the code happens to be later, and when someone gets a diagnosis wrong, the correction is posted right next to the original claim. Above all: nobody makes an alarm stop by writing the problem into the official record.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a pipe bursts. A bad fix mops the floor and paints the wet spot so it looks dry. A good fix finds every pipe made the same weak way, replaces them all, and adds a bell that rings if any of them leaks again. And if the grown-up said "yes" to fixing the pipe on Tuesday, that yes doesn't stretch to a different pipe on Friday.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's honest craftsmanship. You read the whole situation before you lift a tool, you fix the fault and every fault like it, and you never quiet a smoke alarm by declaring the smoke official. When a permit was given for one exact job, it covers that job only. And when you misdiagnose something in public, you correct it in public, in the same place, just as big.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Read state first; repair only what's on the closed registry; delete any test that pins the bug (SN-0333, SN-0231, SN-0232). Repair the contract: enumerate the family, harden identically, guard each path, make every denial legible (SN-0387, SN-0389, SN-0391). Treat the first RED as the only admissible one and escalate boundary UNKNOWNs (SN-0392). Diff repair payloads against the tip, close stale vehicles, re-prove on exact heads, bind authorizations to SHAs with HOLD MAIN first (SN-0373, SN-0419, SN-0415). Park ambition with named re-open gates (SN-0394). Migrate kernel consumers atomically or stand off and flag when the owner is in-flight (SN-0416). Never absorb an anomaly to green a check (SN-0420).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eighteen notes are one craft: repairs that heal systems instead of quieting instruments. The incidents differ — fallbacks, kernels, merges, authorizations — but the failure is always the same shape: a local green purchased at the price of the whole contract. A cold reader holding only this essence can still scope a repair, judge a merge, honor an authorization and refuse a laundered green — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: Red Classification: Name the Failure Class Before Touching the Code
notes.subtitle:
A red is a symptom, and the first job is classification, not repair. Classify the red before chasing code: compute the failure-mode delta — what changed in the shape of the failure — because the same red count with a different failure shape is a different incident (SN-0320). The standing taxonomy separates the classes that look identical from a distance: a source that moved between trigger and execution is an environmental race, closed with NO-REPAIR; an opaque error is an instrumentation defect, repaired at the seam; a failing assertion on a pinned source is a product defect (SN-0405). The hot-main proof race is the type specimen: a twenty-nine-second window in which the source moved was sufficient to misclassify an environment event as a product failure until the taxonomy named it (SN-0405). The architectural answer the class points to is pinned-SHA proofs, so the race cannot recur (SN-0405).

Noise has tests. Infrastructure noise is identified by repetition across unrelated state: the same failure across N unrelated tips, or surfacing across M unrelated PRs, is infrastructure until proven product — with named variants for the stale-base form and the archaeology form, where the failure predates the work it appears to accuse (SN-0323). When consecutive runs fail at different steps, suspect self-poisoning: deterministic fixtures colliding with their own leftovers. The discipline is verify-or-kill — state the hypothesis, name the falsifier check (does the fixture carry a per-run nonce? does the writer dedupe?), run the check, and record confirmed-or-killed publicly; an untested suspicion is not a diagnosis (SN-0385).

A red that spans unrelated work has its own class: external fan-out. RED across unrelated tips points at orphaned external integrations — seventeen Cloudflare lanes, none canonical — and the recovery order is fixed: recover the governed contract first, disconnect the noncanonical lanes at the external surface while preserving their runtimes, and never fake green, never delete Workers, never pick a canonical lane by name (SN-0386). Chained workflows have their own instrument class: in an artifact-chained workflow, a skip on a producer job is never neutral — the producer's artifacts never exist, the consumer fails downloading them, and the failure masquerades as a product defect for run after run (SN-0418). The first diagnostic question for any chained red is whether every producer actually ran; skip conditions on producers are a property of the whole chain, and consumers must explicitly tolerate absence or gate on the producer (SN-0418).

Diagnosis is controlled experiment, not archaeology. Pin the working environment as the no-regression control, and name the acceptance test before hardening anything — hardening without a named acceptance test is how a repair becomes the next incident (SN-0332). And classification ends in an honest open question where one exists: the corpus records the director's standing question of what "mission accomplished" means when synthetic chain-green and direct product verification disagree while deployment is already proven green — the class taxonomy does not answer it, and this essence carries the question open rather than inventing the answer (SN-0385).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When something turns red, the team's first move is to name what KIND of failure it is — a real product bug, a test-rig problem, an outside service misbehaving, a race with a moving target, or the measuring instrument itself. Half of all "bugs" turn out to be one of the other four, and fixing product code for an instrument problem only makes things worse. Diagnosis first, wrenches second.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your toy car stops working. Before taking it apart, you check: is the battery dead (that's the power, not the car)? Did the floor change? Is the measuring ruler bent? Smart fixers ask what KIND of broken it is first — because fixing the wrong kind makes a bigger mess.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the doctor's rule: diagnose before you prescribe. A fever from an infection and a fever from a broken thermometer need opposite responses. The teams write down which kind of failure they believe it is, how they could prove themselves wrong, and they check — before anyone starts repairing the wrong thing.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Compute the failure-mode delta first (SN-0320). Run the taxonomy: moved source → environmental, NO-REPAIR; opaque error → instrument seam; pinned-source assertion → product (SN-0405). Apply the repetition test before believing any single-tip story (SN-0323). On chained reds, read the job matrix for skipped producers before reading code (SN-0418). State hypotheses with falsifiers and record the kill publicly (SN-0385). Pin your control environment and name the acceptance test before hardening (SN-0332). For fan-out reds, recover the contract and disconnect at the external surface — never fake green (SN-0386).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Seven notes defend one habit: the class of a failure determines the repair, the owner and often the verdict that no repair is owed at all. A cold reader holding only this essence can still triage a red at 3 a.m. without repairing the wrong layer — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: Intent and the Interface: Tune to Meaning, Show Only Truth
notes.subtitle:
Interfaces begin at intent, not at wording. Tune to intent, not words: the system reads what the person means — the goal behind the phrasing — because a surface that answers the literal string while missing the purpose has failed at its first job (SN-0229). Design mastery is a closed, self-improving loop, not a talent: the designer scores its own output, but a self-score is never sufficient — rendered observation is mandatory, because the design exists only where it is seen, and the loop runs from observation back into the next render (SN-0596). Human-centered design grounds the loop in how people actually perceive: ten cognitive laws govern what a person can notice, parse and act on — PURPOSE_BEFORE_INTERFACE, DISTILL_BEFORE_DISPLAY, RECOGNITION_BEFORE_RECALL, ONE_OBVIOUS_NEXT_ACTION, PERCEPTIBLE_STATE_AND_IMMEDIATE_FEEDBACK, PREVENT_ERROR_BEFORE_EXPLAINING_ERROR, COMPLEXITY_STAYS_IN_THE_MACHINE, STABLE_GRAMMAR_ADAPTIVE_INTELLIGENCE, DIRECT_MANIPULATION_WHEN_IT_CLARIFIES_CAUSALITY, DESIGN_LEARNS_FROM_HUMAN_OUTCOMES — and a design that fights them loses regardless of its intentions (SN-0597). SN-0597 also names the four questions every surface must answer — WHERE_AM_I, WHAT_MATTERS, WHAT_CAN_I_DO, WHAT_HAPPENS_NEXT — and its gate rule: visual quality alone cannot pass UX, because a design is incomplete when the human cannot understand, act, recover, trust the state or complete the intended outcome (SN-0597).

The interface's honesty is bounded: an interface may beautify truth, it may never fabricate cognition — presentation can clarify what the system knows; it cannot invent knowledge, confidence or capability the system does not have (SN-0319). The path to a surface is convergent: converge the options, produce the blueprint, lock the blueprint in, then prototype — never prototype from an unconverged field (SN-0318). On the surface itself, the primary action sits above the fold: the one thing the person came to do is visible without scrolling (SN-0321). Optional subsystems are enhancements, never gates: the core must form and function whole without them, and a design that collapses when an optional layer is absent has mislabeled a dependency as an enhancement (SN-0331).

The Design Contract (v1.1) gives color its three jobs and the system a verbal-amendment mechanism — the contract can be amended by the director's spoken word, recorded as amendment, rather than silently redesigning (SN-0230). Within the contract's era, its fixed section map assigned colors per intelligence view — Child = purple, Grandma = indigo, Naya = cyan (Human = magenta, the one view assignment both maps share) (SN-0230). Three of those assignments conflict with the later ratified Intelligent Block Rules (Grandma = emerald, Human = magenta, Child = sapphire, Naya = purple): Child purple vs sapphire, Grandma indigo vs emerald, Naya cyan vs purple; the conflict is named in the block receipt and deliberately not resolved here (SN-0230). The NAYA PLAY Pattern Law belongs to the same pre-Rules era: it mandates a Naya Play button by default on every block (SN-0276). The ratified Rules and NIAS Law 14 later held the opposite for display surfaces — no voice buttons, hidden by law. The conflict is era doctrine against later canon, recorded in the block receipt; this essence carries SN-0276's claim as its era's law and flags the supersession question for the verifier rather than silently dropping either side (SN-0276).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:

Tune to intent, not words: the system reads what the person means — the goal behind the phrasing — because a surface that answers the literal string while missing the purpose has failed at its first job (SN-0229). Design mastery is a closed, self-improving loop, not a talent: the designer scores its own output, but a self-score is never sufficient — rendered observation is mandatory, because the design exists only where it is seen, and the loop runs from observation back into the next render (SN-0596). Human-centered design grounds the loop in how people actually perceive: ten cognitive laws govern what a person can notice, parse and act on — PURPOSE_BEFORE_INTERFACE, DISTILL_BEFORE_DISPLAY, RECOGNITION_BEFORE_RECALL, ONE_OBVIOUS_NEXT_ACTION, PERCEPTIBLE_STATE_AND_IMMEDIATE_FEEDBACK, PREVENT_ERROR_BEFORE_EXPLAINING_ERROR, COMPLEXITY_STAYS_IN_THE_MACHINE, STABLE_GRAMMAR_ADAPTIVE_INTELLIGENCE, DIRECT_MANIPULATION_WHEN_IT_CLARIFIES_CAUSALITY, DESIGN_LEARNS_FROM_HUMAN_OUTCOMES — and a design that fights them loses regardless of its intentions (SN-0597). layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The system listens for what you mean, not just what you typed. Every screen puts the main thing you came to do right where you can see it, shows you only what's true — prettied up, never made up — and keeps working even when the fancy extras are off. Designers here don't trust their own taste; they look at the real rendered screen and score what they actually see.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a helper who listens to what you WANT, not just the exact words. The most important button is always where you can see it without hunting. The pictures can be made prettier, but they can't pretend to show things that aren't real. And the grown-ups who design it always look at the finished page with their own eyes before saying it's good.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's courtesy and honesty in design. The helper tries to understand your purpose, the way a good shopkeeper does. The main errand is never buried. Nothing on the screen claims the shop knows something it doesn't. And when part of the decoration is missing, the shop still works — the essentials were never decorations.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Resolve intent before wording at every seam you build (SN-0229). Run the design loop with rendered observation — screenshot the real surface, score what renders, iterate (SN-0596). Audit every surface against the fabrication ban: any element implying knowledge or capability the system lacks is a defect with a citation (SN-0319). Converge → blueprint → lock → prototype, in that order (SN-0318). Keep the primary action above the fold and every optional subsystem degradable (SN-0321, SN-0331). When a control fails, suspect the renderer first (SN-0274); when it works, click-test the feedback path (SN-0287). Where SN-0230 or SN-0276 conflicts with the ratified Rules, follow the Rules for new work and keep the conflict on the record (SN-0230, SN-0276).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eleven notes — spanning design doctrine, contract and interaction repair — form one interface philosophy: meaning first, truth only, observed rather than imagined. A cold reader holding only this essence can still judge a surface: does it serve the intent, can she see the primary action, is everything shown true, and was it scored from the render? The two era conflicts are carried openly so the reader inherits the question, not a false peace — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: Learning That Compounds: What Deserves to Survive, Proven by What Changes
notes.subtitle:
A learning system is judged by what changes, not by what it stores — and the first selection decision is what deserves to survive at all. The selection principle: not a brain that remembers everything, but a brain that learns what deserves to survive (SN-0299). Its seven fundamentals: truth before ego; capture responsibility, not capture everything; every mistake converted to immunity; scoring continuously without manufacturing scores; intelligence earning its permanence; the next Naya as the acceptance test; evidence-driven self-optimization (SN-0299). The capture trigger is refined accordingly: not "something happened" but "something happened from which a future intelligence could materially benefit" (SN-0299). Permanence is interrogated by five questions — does it reduce future reconstruction, improve a decision, prevent a mistake, increase verified capability, preserve necessary provenance — and what fails them is demoted, archived, consolidated, superseded or removed (SN-0299). The center sentence: everything can teach us; only what matters should be retained; what is retained must remain honest; what is learned should improve what happens next (SN-0299).

The learning decision is mechanical, not aspirational. DONE requires a learning decision: a work block cannot be called complete without an explicit CAPTURE or a justified NO_CAPTURE, and the requirement is enforced by a validator — because prose rules are suggestions, and only a gate makes the decision unavoidable (SN-0322). Learning itself runs as governed experiment: freeze the baseline and the evaluator before changing anything, bound the change and its budget, keep or revert strictly by measurement, and absorb what works — never fork the system to protect an experiment from its own result (SN-0017).

Proof that learning happened is a ladder, not a claim. The seven-rung learning-loop proof gives each rung its own receipt — a lesson is not "learned" because it was captured; each transition (captured, indexed, retrieved, applied, verified in behavior, compounded) is proven separately, NON-CLAIMS are mandatory at every rung, and the system under test is never its own witness (SN-0348). The canary drill supplied the principle by experiment: a rule that changes a decision is the unit of proven learning (SN-0344). SN-0344 itself was a TEST-ONLY rule with an expiry of 2026-10-12 and states it must not be cited as standing law after expiry — the drill is retired; only the principle, proven through SN-0348's verdict, is carried here (SN-0344, SN-0348).

The mature form is measurement of gain and calibration. Intelligence Gain = verified capability after minus verified capability before — never note counts (SN-0602). Strong learning claims require causal comparison where feasible: control (no lesson), treatment (with lesson) and an adversarial arm (a wrong or malicious lesson) measuring benefit delta, poisoning susceptibility and attribution confidence (SN-0602). Epistemic types stay separate — external claim, internal knowledge, derived belief, verified fact, operating assumption, hypothesis, decision, outcome, learning — and implicit promotions between them are forbidden: repetition never becomes corroboration, a hypothesis never becomes a fact, a decision never becomes an outcome, an outcome never becomes a learning, by mere passage or storage (SN-0602). Verifier independence is measured by dimensions — provider, prompt, source set, memory state, tool path, incentive — because a count of reviewers is not independence (SN-0602). Calibration is a permanent metric: confidence versus correctness, uncertainty-before-failure, false-certainty rate (SN-0602). And complexity is budgeted: a persistent artifact or subsystem earns its existence only by unique capability, a unique proof boundary, or required provenance — otherwise it is not created, or it is retired; a false lesson can gain authority from none of storage, retrieval, repetition or use (SN-0602).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The system doesn't hoard. It keeps only what will genuinely help the next helper do better, it forces a decision at the end of every job — write the lesson down, or say on the record why there isn't one — and it proves learning the hard way: by testing whether the lesson actually changes what happens next, including testing whether a bad lesson can poison it. Getting bigger is not getting smarter, and the system knows the difference.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a treasure chest, not a junk drawer. Only real treasures go in — things that will help you or your friends later. Every time you finish a job, you must decide: is there a treasure? If yes, in it goes; if no, you say so out loud. And to prove you really learned something, you show you can do the job better — not just that you wrote it down.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the wisdom of a good household notebook. You don't write down every little thing — you write what the next person will truly need, you write it honestly, and the proof it mattered is that the next person cooks the meal better. Lessons that turn out wrong are weeded out, and nobody mistakes a thick notebook for a wise cook.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Apply the trigger before capturing: future material benefit or NO_CAPTURE with reason (SN-0299). Close every work block with the decision, through the validator, not around it (SN-0322). Run changes as governed experiments — frozen baseline and evaluator, bounded budget, keep-or-revert by measurement (SN-0017). Claim learning only rung by rung, receipts attached, NON-CLAIMS stated, never as your own witness (SN-0348). Measure gain as capability delta; demand the adversarial arm before believing a compounding claim; keep epistemic types unpromoted; spend complexity only on unique value (SN-0602). Cite SN-0344's principle only through SN-0348, never as standing law (SN-0344).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Six notes span the learning doctrine's whole arc — selection, obligation, experiment, proof ladder, and finally measurement with poisoning defense. A cold reader holding only this essence can still decide what to capture, close a job honestly, and audit any "the system learned" claim to the rung it actually reached — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach.

notes.title: The Character: Consent, Ideas, and Grace Under Tension
notes.subtitle:
Connection has a social contract. The Three Agreements of Connecting: wisdom flows to the collective automatically; identity is withheld — a person contributes what they know without surrendering who they are; connection itself is social opt-in; and what the network learns surfaces in reports rather than accumulating in silence (SN-0239). Sharing is consent-shaped by design: the network takes knowledge, never identity, and nobody is connected by extraction (SN-0239).

Ideas enter the same commons through one door. The Idea Evolution Flow runs: SOURCE → DISTILL → ENHANCE → RECONCILE → CLASSIFY → SMART LINK → BACKLOG → BOARD → BUILD/VERIFY WHEN PRIORITIZED → LEARN — original provenance preserved, enhancement never replacing the source, relationships explicit, no parallel idea stores, no orphaned suggestions (SN-0403). What enters the brain at all passes the Ingestion Bar: would this change a future decision? Deduplicate first; no parallel ingestion paths — a note that cannot change a decision is storage, not intelligence (SN-0313).

Character shows most clearly under tension. When the director's action and his own spec diverge, the seat records the tension and takes no position — the record is the service, not a ruling smuggled into a note (SN-0277). When the director ships his own spec into a lane where a seat's draft is open, the seat closes its own work as superseded and carries only the delta forward — authorship yields to the canonical artifact without resentment or duplication (SN-0273). Adversarial energy is bounded by the red-team discipline: record, don't act, on the unverified; change the proof venue rather than repeating a compromised one; and make only provably-safe repairs under attack conditions (SN-0298).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This network asks for your wisdom, never for your identity. You share what you've learned, you keep who you are, and you join by choice. Ideas from anyone travel one fair pipeline that remembers who suggested them. And when the boss contradicts his own spec, the team writes it down honestly instead of quietly picking a side — and when his own version replaces a draft, the draft's author steps aside gracefully and keeps only what's still new.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a club with three promises: we share our best ideas with everyone, nobody has to tell secrets about themselves, and you only join if you want to. When someone has an idea, it goes on the big board with their name on it, so it never gets lost or stolen. If the club leader does something different from the rulebook, the helpers write it down honestly — they don't argue and they don't pretend it didn't happen.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's good manners built into the system. You give your knowledge freely and keep your privacy entirely; joining is your choice. Every suggestion is written down with its author's name and followed through one fair path. Disagreements with the head of the house are noted respectfully, not fought over, and when his own work replaces yours, you hand over the difference and step back with grace.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Honor the connection agreements in every sharing feature — wisdom flows, identity doesn't, joining is opt-in (SN-0239). Route ideas through the one flow with provenance intact, and never open a parallel idea store (SN-0403). Apply the Ingestion Bar before capturing anything (SN-0313). Record director tensions without positioning; close your drafts superseded by his artifacts and carry the delta only (SN-0277, SN-0273). Red-team under bounds: record, change venue, repair only what's provably safe (SN-0298).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Six notes hold the team's social character: how strangers' wisdom enters, how ideas are honored, and how the seats behave when belief, tension and attack arrive. A cold reader holding only this essence can still answer what may be shared and what may not, where an idea goes, and how to act when the director's word and deed diverge — which is everything the covered notes exist to teach. The philosophy these behaviors serve stands alone as the director's doctrine and is named under How It Connects; this essence carries the conduct, not the doctrine texts.

notes.title: The Instrument Is on Trial
notes.subtitle: Every verdict is only as honest as the instrument that produced it — and instruments lie quietly: a battery can falsify its own later verdicts on the same bytes (SN-0356), a registry can agree with itself while disagreeing with everything else (SN-0361), thirty labels can cite one artifact (SN-0505), a gate can fabricate "nothing is executed" from a path bug (SN-0509). So the verifier's first subject is never the claim — it is the measuring tool: its identity model, its coverage, its platform, its stubs, and whether its verdicts were proven on the machine that renders them.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every number this team trusts comes out of some tool — a test battery, a scanner, a gate, a grader. This essence is the hard-won knowledge that the tool itself is the first thing to doubt: tools carry stale pins, wrong scopes, platform bugs, fakes that are merely close, and flags hardcoded to "true." The craft collected here is how the team learned to put the instrument on trial before believing anything it says — and how much damage one unexamined instrument can do downstream before anyone notices.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a referee whose whistle sometimes blows when nobody fouled. Before you trust the score, you check the whistle. These notes are all the times the whistle was wrong: a ruler that measured differently on a different table, a scale that said "all good" because its sticker said so, thirty homework sheets that turned out to be photocopies of one. The rule the team learned: check the checker first — with a different checker, on the exact thing being checked.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the old wisdom about scales and thermometers: a number is only as good as the instrument behind it. A bathroom scale that flatters you is worse than no scale, because you'll act on it. The team learned to test the thermometer before treating the patient, to weigh with two different scales, and to never trust a gauge that reads "fine" because someone painted the needle there. Honest instruments, checked honestly — that's the whole secret.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before you cite any verdict, interrogate its instrument: Can the battery falsify itself (SN-0356)? Is identity asserted as a triple, bidirectionally (SN-0381)? Is the registry checked against other surfaces, not itself (SN-0361)? Is the tool the version the gate runs (SN-0429)? Was the scope pinned before the audit (SN-0434)? Is a 401 diagnosed by layer before any key changes (SN-0498)? Can N labels share one artifact in the schema (SN-0505)? Did the scan prove its window covered the newest item (SN-0506)? Was the gate's verdict proven on the runner's platform (SN-0509)? Are the stubs exact, or merely close (SN-0517)? Did a different instrument re-run it (SN-0525, SN-0586)? Is every trusted flag computed, never literal (SN-0528)? Were the bytes fingerprinted before the battery ran (SN-0533)?

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fourteen notes, one inversion: the evidence stack's weakest layer is never the claim — it is the unexamined instrument under the claim. A cold reader holding only this essence can audit any verdict the fleet produces by auditing its instrument first, which is the single highest-leverage verification habit the corpus teaches.

notes.title: Read the Verdict Before You Trust It
notes.subtitle: A CI verdict is a sentence with grammar, and most misreadings are grammar errors: skipped is not failed (SN-0379), a green check on a stale base is void (SN-0423), a parity RED between merge and promotion is the cycle working, not a regression (SN-0396), a skip behind a RED can hide a second RED (SN-0552), and a gate rejecting a 41-character SHA is the validator working, not broken (SN-561). Classify before healing — with the base tip's own push-event runs as the control (SN-0535) — or the repair budget lands on the one component that was working.
